html:
Ninticoy is the map's spelling of the Nanticoke, an Algonquian people of the Eastern Shore of Chesapeake Bay, in what are now Maryland and Delaware. Their name means "people of the tidewater".

They farmed maize, fished and gathered oysters along the rivers of the Delmarva Peninsula. Captain John Smith met them in 1608. When English Maryland was founded in 1634, settlers spread onto their lands, and the colony fought them several times. In the mid-1700s many Nanticoke moved north up the Susquehanna and joined the Haudenosaunee and the Lenape, and later went on to Canada and Oklahoma. Others stayed, and the Nanticoke Indian Tribe of Millsboro, Delaware, remains. See Nentego and their neighbours the Conoy.
sum: Ninticoy is the map's spelling of the Nanticoke, an Algonquian people of the Eastern Shore of Chesapeake Bay, in what are now Maryland and Delaware. Their name means "people of the tidewater".
